title: .NET Technical Screening – Round 1
description: Welcome, and thank you for your interest in this role. Most questions show a code snippet or scenario. Read each one carefully and write your answer in your own words in the box below it.
instructions: Assume .NET 8 and C# 12 unless a question says otherwise.
Answer independently, without running the code, searching online, or using AI tools.
Explain your reasoning, not just the final answer. Partial answers with clear thinking still earn credit.
notice: **How your answers are evaluated:** our interview team reviews every response, and we use AI to help assess the answers. Final decisions are always made by people.

questions.title: The high-value transaction that skipped validation

blocks.text: A payments team has this base class in a shared NuGet package:
A new team writes:

questions.ask: Why didn't the new rule fire? What is the minimum change to the base class and the derived class to fix it?

questions.ask: Walk through the exact construction order and name which field is null and why. Then propose a design that keeps the "initialize hook" idea but is safe.

questions.title: Rate-change notifications in a long-running service

blocks.text: A rate-change notification service:

`RateService` is a **singleton**. `QuoteWidget` is created per user session. After a week of uptime: memory grows monotonically, and a single downstream subscriber throwing an exception means **later subscribers never get the event**.

questions.ask: Diagnose both problems. Then redesign — and justify whether you'd keep `event`, move to `IObservable<T>`, or use a message bus/channel.

questions.title: Reviewing a constructor with many parameters

blocks.text: A teammate adds an 11th optional parameter to this constructor:
Call sites in the wild look like:

blocks.code: new HttpRequestSpec("https://api/x", "POST", 60, true, 5, "application/json", false, token, true, 5, true);

questions.ask: Name three concrete failure modes of this design as it exists today. Then show how a Builder (or a modern C# alternative) fixes them — and say when a Builder would be *over-engineering* here.

questions.title: Pick the right collection

blocks.text: For each scenario, name the structure and justify in one line:

rows: Deduplicate 2 million loan numbers read from a file; you only need "have I seen this?"
Map `loanNumber → LoanSummary`, single-threaded batch job, ~10k entries, need fastest lookup
Same map, but read and written by 200 concurrent request threads
Need to answer "give me all loans with amount between 200k and 500k, in order" repeatedly
A cache where you must evict the least-recently-used entry when you hit 10,000 items

blocks.text: This ran fine against 500 test records and times out against 80,000 production records:

questions.title: One library, three apps, one hangs

blocks.text: The same library method is consumed by three apps. It deadlocks in one of them.

questions.ask: Which consumers deadlock, and which don't? Explain the mechanism precisely. Would `ConfigureAwait(false)` in the library fix it? Should the library add it anyway? And what's the correct fix in each consumer?

questions.title: Program.cs after a cleanup

blocks.text: A developer reorders `Program.cs` while "cleaning up":

Reported symptoms: every `[Authorize]` endpoint returns **401 even with a valid token**, unhandled exceptions return a raw stack trace instead of the error page, and static files are served but slowly.

questions.ask: Give the correct order and explain, for each symptom, which ordering mistake causes it.

questions.title: Service registrations and a data mix-up

blocks.text: The app starts fine in Development but throws at startup in Production. Later, after a "fix," reports intermittently contain **another user's** data.

questions.ask: Explain the startup difference between environments, name the anti-pattern, and describe exactly how the cross-user data leak happens. Then fix both registrations properly.

questions.title: Active-loans report that's fast locally, slow in production

blocks.text: Local (200 loans): 400ms. Production (45,000 active loans): 3-minute timeout, and the DBA reports **hundreds of thousands** of queries from this endpoint.

questions.ask: Name the problem and count the queries. Rewrite it. Then: your rewrite uses `Include` — explain when `Include` is the *wrong* answer here and what you'd do instead. Finally, what would you add so this can never regress silently?

questions.title: Request counter that miscounts under load

blocks.text: A multi-tenant API tracks request counts:
Two production defects are reported:

items: `TenantMetrics.Increment()` returns duplicate values and the final total is **lower** than actual requests under load.

A developer "fixed" it by switching to `OrderMetrics<T>` and now `OrderMetrics<Retail>.Increment()` and `OrderMetrics<Wholesale>.Increment()` return **independent** sequences — which they did not expect.

questions.ask: Explain both behaviors precisely. Then: what's the correct primitive for #1, and is #2 a bug or a feature you could exploit?

questions.title: Making an inherited API deployable

blocks.text: You inherit a .NET 8 API that "works on my machine" and is deployed by copying files onto a VM and restarting it. You're asked to make it deploy safely and repeatably. Here's what you find:
Also: in-memory session state, logs written to `C:\app\logs\app.log`, a hardcoded `if (Environment.MachineName == "PROD-WEB-01")` branch, and no health endpoint.

questions.ask: List what must change before this can be deployed automatically to multiple environments and more than one instance. Group your answer by concern, and say which single change you'd make first.
